public_rationale: JLL reported on January 6, 2026 that average grid connection lead times exceeded four years in primary markets, supporting lengthy delivery constraints [e1]. For Q1 2026, Amazon, Microsoft and Google accounted for 57% of hyperscale capacity [e2]. That measure does not establish whether Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta and OpenAI held or reserved most global usable AI capacity without overlapping allocations [e2]. Neither item documents that Amazon, Microsoft and Google each supplied both Anthropic and OpenAI, so the full claim remains unresolved [e1, e2].
limitations: Hyperscale capacity is not a matched denominator for either global usable AI capacity or all data-center capacity.
The evidence lacks non-overlapping owner and customer allocations for the five firms.
Grid connection lead times do not measure every project's construction duration.
The packet does not establish every stated supplier relationship.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Global data center capacity is limited and slow to build, and most of it is taken by Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta and OpenAI.

statement.excerpt: Remember: data centers take forever to build, and there’s only a limited amount of global capacity, most of which is taken up by Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta and OpenAI, with the first three of those already providing capacity to both Anthropic and OpenAI.

from_speaker: data centers take forever to build
a limited amount of global capacity
most of which is taken up by Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta and OpenAI
the first three of those already providing capacity to both Anthropic and OpenAI
our_interpretation: Forever is ordinary emphasis for lengthy construction and commissioning lead times, not a claim that completion is impossible.
The surrounding discussion makes usable AI data-center capacity the principal denominator. All data-center capacity is a plausible alternative reading.
Taken up includes owned or reserved operational capacity, counted once when a cloud provider supplies another named company.
Use January through March 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter before publication, for this ongoing industry observation.
The supplier statement is a subsidiary factual element; it does not itself establish the global majority.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous global inventories show that the five named firms collectively hold or reserve more than half of usable AI capacity without double counting, and demonstrate material constraints and long delivery times. The stated supplier relationships must also be documented.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A comparable global inventory places the five firms at half or less, or representative evidence shows abundant promptly deliverable capacity inconsistent with the claimed constraints. A disproved supplier relationship would contradict that subsidiary element.

evidence.excerpt: grid connection lead times exceeding four years
evidence.explanation: Supports the delivery-constraint and lengthy-lead-time elements. Grid connection time is not identical to physical construction time and this finding does not establish company concentration.

evidence.excerpt: 57% of all hyperscale data center capacity
evidence.locator: Which Companies Lead Global Hyperscale Datacenter Capacity?
evidence.explanation: The three are Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, and the article identifies the underlying inventory as Q1 2026. This supports concentration within hyperscale infrastructure, but cannot establish the same share of all global AI capacity.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A Q1 2026 global operational AI-capacity inventory with consistent units and non-overlapping allocations to the five firms, alongside dated delivery records and documentation of each stated supplier relationship.
